result.title: Junction Geometry Survives an Unidentifiable Blur
result.summary: Thin filaments cross in microscopy, and dispersed spectra cross on X-ray detectors. At a junction, where these structures cross or branch, how many straight arms meet, and which way do they go? Unknown blur obscures the answer. At a balanced crossing, distinct Gaussian blurs can even produce the same observation law. We show that the arms can still be recovered. For separated rays of nonvanishing weight and an unknown centered Gaussian-mixture blur, a distance combining arm count, directions, relative weights and supporting lines is bounded by a constant times the Euclidean difference in cell probabilities on a sufficiently fine fixed grid. The bound is uniform over a bounded model class, including unidentifiable blurs. From $n$ positions or photon counts, the minimax error is of order $n^{-1/2}$. This rate is proved for a global estimator. In practice we fit rays and blur by constrained local likelihood, reducing the BIC count when two detectors agree on fewer arms in the microscopy studies. Across three studies with protocols fixed before evaluation, on 360 crossings and branches assembled from measured single-molecule localizations, the fit gets the arm count and every direction within $10^\circ$ 24 to 37 percentage points more often than a tuned fixed-scale Hessian ridge detector, averaged over 25 to 400 localizations. On acute angles with correct counts, mean absolute error is $3.5^\circ$ to $4.3^\circ$, versus $10.4^\circ$ to $15.5^\circ$. On Chandra spectra, 38 of 90 fits at 800 photons find all four arms within $10^\circ$; among these, median error is $0.023^\circ$.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在未知高斯混合模糊下，如何从显微或 X 射线探测器上的交叉、分叉节点恢复直臂的数量、方向、相对权重与支撑直线；给出在含不可辨识模糊的有界模型类上的一致误差上界与 n^{-1/2} 极小极大速率，并用带约束的局部似然拟合在显微与 Chandra 光谱数据上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对「不可辨识模糊」下几何结构仍可恢复的可辨识性与误差界刻画，可能与 LVR 关注的视觉细节是否保留在内部状态、以及观测退化时几何证据的可辨识性与筛选问题相关，概念线索可供核查，但需人工判断能否迁移。
